commits.summary: jvmcontract: claims javac compiles, String and String[] inputs, String, stream and regex models, induction and lemmas, for example 286's decision claim (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 286 (CVE-2022-22968, Spring Framework 5.3.18 to 5.3.19) states its decision claim in Java over the adapter entry allowed(String[] allowedPatterns, String[] disallowedPatterns, String field): a field some disallowed pattern matches ignoring ASCII case is denied, the match written with streams, lambdas and java.util.regex. Until now jvmcontract refused it at the String[] parameters, at the expressions, and at every String, StringBuilder, stream and regex call on the way. With this change the unchanged claim is proved on 5.3.19 and refuted on 5.3.18 and on the constructed mutant at small bounds inline (3 code units and 3 elements: 8 s, 7 s and 6 s in an unoptimized build), each witness run in the harness on a JVM; the frozen bound of 8 is queued.

What a property check gained. A String parameter is a String of its own of at most --max-array-length code units, and a String[] an array of such Strings or nulls. An assumption or assertion the tool's own expression compiler does not take is compiled by javac into a class beside the harness and run as bytecode, as the target is; a witness of such a claim is run in the harness on a JVM, so a refutation rests on Java's own libraries and not on a model. prove --decreases EXPR proves a method that calls itself by induction on a measure: a recursive call on arguments within the assumption and the bound whose measure is smaller is taken to satisfy the property, and any other recursive call ends the check with no verdict. prove --lemmas FILE proves each lemma first and then lets its statement stand in for the calls of its method where the arguments are within the bound it was proved at, the method running as written elsewhere; a method that writes a field or compares its arguments by identity is refused as a lemma's subject.

What the own checker gained. String.substring, indexOf, endsWith, toLowerCase on ASCII (under the stated assumption that the default locale is not Turkish, Azeri or Lithuanian), split at one character and chars; StringBuilder's constructors, length, indexOf, substring, delete and toString; lambdas, method references and four stream model classes run as the loops they stand for; Pattern.quote, String.join, Pattern.compile, matcher and matches as far as a claim states a glob with them, a pattern held as its pieces so that a case-insensitive match and an exact match of lower-cased Strings are one formula; class literals, Class.forName and the class path's loader under a stated assumption, for spring-jcl's logging probes. Each new String method has an evidence record in values::OPERATIONS (String model 3) whose 85 boundary cases give one outcome on the JVM, in the interpreter and in the checker; the interpreter's substring and toLowerCase now return the JDK's objects (the String itself, the literal empty String). What a model takes for granted about the JVM is listed among a statement's assumptions.

Paths. Once more than 1024 paths have been explored (Options::merge_heaps_after), paths whose heaps are not of one shape are merged into the union of their heaps, each first rid of dead locals and unreachable objects; a loop's exit is then a join, and waiting paths are resumed in the order of the loops they are in. Below that count the engine merges as before. The count is a measured compromise: merging heaps from the first path took the values sweep's list totals from 0.07 s to over a minute at 6 lines, since the two sums are then no longer one formula by gate hashing, and waiting for 1024 paths costs example 286's decision 1.7 times its time at 5 code units against 512. An array of computed size is taken within one more than the bound (a table over a bounded String's positions).

Two leaks found by the default run and closed. The new StringBuilder, Class and ArrayList models had been added to gaps::exact_jdk_call, which JBMC's gap listing and the contract reader also ask: JBMC's stubs for those calls would have counted as exact, and a contract for StringBuilder.<init>() was refused. They are now gaps::modelled_jdk_call, the own checker's alone, and a contract given for a modelled call is applied in place of the model, so the three contract tests of lib/tests/integration.rs pass unchanged. And a call the checker has no model of on a builder it holds the content of (append, reverse) now drops that content: a later modelled call on the builder is refused by name instead of answering from stale content.

examples/286-.../proofs/prove.py TASK runs vulnerable-security, fixed-security or mutant-security from target.json and the frozen claim file, on the revision's pinned JARs (each checked against its SHA-256) with the adapter compiled against them, and builds the mutant as sources.lock.json says. proofs/simple-match.contract is the lemma: PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch on ASCII Strings is the claim's own regular expression, by induction on the pattern's length. These are proofs beside the example route, which runs the verifier on the original artifact alone and still stops at DataBinder's receiver (VF-027); the example's records are not changed in this commit and follow with the results.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: loops beyond the bound covered by invariants, constant regexes, text as bytes and digits, for example 287's bcrypt claims (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 287 (CVE-2025-22228: BCrypt.hashpw ignores bytes past 72) asks whether checkpw rejects a password of more than 72 bytes for every valid stored hash. The tool's own checker stopped at the claim's regular expression, at the text-to-bytes calls and at bcrypt's loops, which go round 18, 512, 2^cost and 64 times against --unwind 16. It now runs the claims as they are written. A loop that goes round more often than the bound is covered by an invariant the checker finds and proves by induction (lib/src/bmc/loops.rs: what one iteration writes is set to any value, candidate facts about each written number are dropped until the rest is kept by an iteration, and the loop is shown to end by a counter or said not to be); a verdict names the loops so covered, a violation past one is believed only when its witness, the least violating input, reproduces on a JVM, and otherwise the answer is no verdict with the loop named. Also new: String.matches and Pattern.compile of a constant regular expression with classes, groups, alternatives and counts (lib/src/bmc/regex.rs); String.getBytes(UTF_8), MessageDigest.isEqual, Arrays.copyOf, Integer.parseInt and StringBuilder's charAt and appends (lib/src/bmc/bytes.rs, strings.rs); Object.getClass of an object the run made, String.toString, an initializer that keeps method references, and a throws clause whose condition javac compiles. The solver side defers clauses until a call depends on them, checks lazy divisions only in the cone a question reads, and shares a path's models by pages. The search for the least witness takes at most half the time the run has left, so a violation found late is not lost to it.

The String model is model 4, the reference calls model 2: getBytes, matches and toString have evidence records sampled on the JVM and in the checker (lib/tests/values.rs), the gap scan counts Pattern.compile of a constant in the checker's syntax as reproduced, and the interpreter's String.toString returns the String itself. Tests that relied on a class regex, toString or a builder append being a gap now use forms that still are (a reluctant or possessive quantifier, trim, append(CharSequence), append(long)); the calibration fixture's RegexGate uses a possessive quantifier and its records were remade. New tests: lib/tests/loops.rs (four, on a small fixture with the same loop shapes), three in lib/tests/claims.rs (each model against a definition written out in Java and sampled on a JVM), three unit tests in bits.rs. Verified inline by the default run (python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run: 34 of 34 passed).

Example 287 has proofs/prove.py, which runs the three security tasks beside the route through the adapter entry the claim names, and a dated note. One capped probe (5 minutes, 4 GiB) proved the byte-array guard claim on 6.3.8 at the route's bound in 250 s with six loops covered; the probe on 6.3.7 found its violating path and ran out of time minimising the witness, and the probe of the security claim through the adapter did not finish. commits.summary: Two modes of a checkout: development, and runtime on a user's machine
commits.body:
/prove-java-change will install a released copy of this repository on a user's machine. That copy must not trace, redact or publish anything, yet the agents working in it follow this repository's procedure, which says to commit with sync.py commit. So the procedure stays one and the checkout decides: llm-dlc/tools/mode.py tells a runtime checkout by a marker file at its root, .in-the-loop-runtime.json (written by the skill's bootstrap, gitignored, a fact about one copy), and anything else is a development checkout that behaves as it always has. IN_THE_LOOP_MODE overrides the marker for tests. A marker that can't be read is an error, never a development checkout, since tracing a user's sessions by mistake would publish them.

In a runtime checkout sync.py does this, decided before it takes its lock or writes anything under its state folder: commit writes the message with an In-The-Loop-Runtime: VERSION sha256:DIGEST trailer naming the release and starts a new change, reading no session; check passes with nothing to check; the hooks that run after every tool call and turn return at once; and every other command (push, upload, scan, sync, review, allow, stamp, langfuse, unpublish, regenerate) refuses and points at llm-dlc/runtime.md. In a development checkout one thing changes: link_commits never stamps a session's trace on a commit that carries the runtime trailer, so a contribution merged from a user's checkout is not credited to whichever session happened to be running when it was authored.

llm-dlc/runtime.md is the new page for the runtime side, starting with the two modes and the procedure for agents in a runtime checkout; CLAUDE.md and llm-dlc/README.md point at it. Examples added in a runtime checkout take numbers 900 to 999, which examples/README.md now reserves, so an update never brings an example with the same number.

Verified: test_mode.py (13 tests, in the cost inventory as unit tier) covers the marker, the override, each runtime command, main's dispatch without the lock, and the unstamped contributed commit. Run for real with IN_THE_LOOP_MODE=runtime: check exits 0, push exits 2 with the reason, hook exits 0 silently. Every Python suite passes (lib/tools/test_costs.py run --only python, 34 of 34 after test_performance.py's copied tool sources gained mode.py), and cargo test --test tiers, the Rust half of the tier lint. The rest of cargo test was not run again: no Rust file changed since the previous commit's full default run.

commits.summary: A release process with a hash, and the bootstrap that installs a release
commits.body:
/prove-java-change runs on a released copy of this repository, and the copy has to be the one the running skill was released with. A release is therefore one commit, the skill at a version and the repository beside it, pinned to each other by the sha256 digest of the commit's tree, which the skill carries in release.json beside its bootstrap. The pin can't name the commit's id, because it is in that commit, so it names the content: the digest is over one line per file (mode, sha256 of its bytes, path) and leaves out the pin itself and the files sync.py regenerates on every commit (llm-dlc/traces/, llm-dlc/index.json, llm-dlc/README.md), which the pin lists. It is of content only, so the trace lines sync.py adds to a commit's message later leave it as it was.

llm-dlc/tools/release.py cut [VERSION] is the one command a release takes, at any commit and as often as wanted: it writes the version into the plugin and the marketplace, the pin from @'s tree, commits with sync.py commit, and verifies the commit; it refuses while @ holds other uncommitted work. status and verify read the last release back. A release reaches users only when main is pushed with it.

plugins/in-the-loop/skills/prove-java-change/bootstrap.py is the user's side and the one implementation of the digest (release.py loads it). status says where things stand as JSON, install clones the repository with jj into IN_THE_LOOP_HOME (by default ~/.local/share/in-the-loop) and stands on the release, update fetches and rebases the user's commits onto the next release, listing conflicts. A release is found without a tag: through the history of the pin, for the commit that carries this version and digest, accepted only when its tree hashes to the digest again. A checkout is current only when that holds, the working copy descends from the release, and the skill's files in the release are the bytes of the skill that is running. Inside a development checkout the bootstrap answers development and installs nothing. The plugin's manifest and the marketplace entry come back with it, as plugin in-the-loop at 0.4.0; the skill's own page follows in a later commit, and no release is cut yet.

commits.summary: feature-loop.sh: a templated moonshot keeps an item for as many cycles as it takes, until a judge outside the session finds it finished, and "item" stops the loop once the item under way is
commits.body:
At the user's request: complex examples can take more than one cycle, but a templated moonshot gave each item exactly one, moving on as soon as a cycle committed (prove-examples left 286 with tasks open), and "stop" could only end the loop after a cycle, not after an example.

Now, after each commit of a templated moonshot, a judge outside the session decides whether the item is finished: a separate claude -p call (FEATURE_LOOP_JUDGE_MODEL, claude-sonnet-5-5 by default) with no tools, only the user's settings and no transcript reads the cycle's final report and commit messages and answers ITEM: finished (the goal is met, or what is left needs a person or only waits on jobs) or ITEM: continue (the session itself can still make real progress). Nothing is added to the moonshot's own session, so its instruction stays the only thing it is given. An unfinished item gets the next cycle with the same instruction; an unclear answer moves on, as before. The record keeps the verdict and its reason under each commit line, and a later run resumes at the first item that has no commit or whose last verdict was continues. FEATURE_LOOP_ITEM_CYCLES caps an item's cycles in a run (no cap by default, the user's choice), and FEATURE_LOOP_ITEM_JUDGE=0 restores one cycle per item. Typing "item" in the loop's terminal ends the run once the item under way is finished, however many cycles that takes; a count typed after it replaces it. loop_stats.py reads the new record header and verdicts, so an item the judge left open counts as attempted, not done, and the verdict is not published as a column.

Verified: test_loop_stats (22, two new) and test_runs pass, and the cost lint agrees. commits.summary: feature-loop.sh: a conductor judges each cycle, an item that waits on its proof lets the next one start, and the loop asks before it changes items
commits.body:
This folds the moonshot branch into the /prove-java-change line. The commit below this one is a duplicate of tlzowkqv (workspace moonshot: an item keeps a templated moonshot until a judge outside the session finds it finished), with its six conflicts against this line resolved; this commit reconciles and extends it. The user asked on 2026-11-16 for everything about moonshot loops from the moonshot and conductor branches to be folded in here, for the loop to be run by a watcher session, and for a loop that goes on while an example waits on its final proof.

With a conductor directory (LOOP_CONDUCTOR, which prove-loop.sh sets) the conductor is the judge: after each commit the loop asks it whether the item is finished, takes another cycle, or only waits on the verification jobs it queued, and falls back on tlzowkqv's own judge (Sonnet, now with the third answer) when no verdict comes in FEATURE_LOOP_JUDGE_WAIT seconds. An item that waits is left: the loop takes the next one meanwhile, and whenever it leaves an item it first returns to the earliest waiting one whose jobs are in (conductor.py unfinished reads the queue and matches jobs to examples by their outputs or title). When only waiting items are left it waits for the first to come in. FEATURE_LOOP_CONTINUE_WHILE_PROVING=0, or prove-loop.sh --wait-for-proofs, keeps the loop on the item instead; the default is on. commits.summary: feature-loop.sh: a templated moonshot keeps an item for as many cycles as it takes, until a judge outside the session finds it finished, and "item" stops the loop once the item under way is

FEATURE_LOOP_ITEM_CYCLES caps an item's cycles in a run (no cap by default, the user's choice), and FEATURE_LOOP_ITEM_JUDGE=0 restores one cycle per item. commits.summary: JBMC runs get a second attempt on Z3 with multiplication congruence lemmas, for VF-018 (verification pending)
commits.body:
Three regression proofs over objects (objects.Kernel#price, lines.Lines#reprice, orders.Orders#reprice) never finished under JBMC within 1800 s: finding VF-018, open since 2026-11-07. Each relates products whose operands are equal only under the correspondence or a branch, such as cents * quantity against quantity * cents. JBMC's SAT backend builds every multiplication as a circuit of its own, so its solver has to find each equality through two 64-bit multipliers. The diagnosis came from another agent's analysis the user passed on; it was reproduced here before anything was built on it: Z3 gives no answer in 60 s on JBMC's formula for the lines case and answers unsat at once with the lemmas, and with JBMC driving Z3 the three proofs take 0.11 to 0.14 s.

The change is in the tool, not in the tests or the harness. lib/src/congruence.rs reads a formula JBMC wrote as SMT-LIB and adds, for every two products of one width, the lemma that equal operands in either order give equal products, which holds of any fixed-width multiplication; nothing else in the formula changes. jbmc::run uses it as a second attempt: a run still without a verdict after a twentieth of its limit (5 s at least, 30 s at most) is held still with SIGSTOP (tla::run_with_interlude), JBMC writes its formula, and JBMC runs again with a solver script that answers that one formula, byte for byte, by giving Z3 the formula with the lemmas. Only a proof with every property holding is taken. Then the result names what decided it (its checker reads 'JBMC 6.11.0, its formula decided by Z3 5.3.3 with 6 multiplication congruence lemma(s)', its evidence names Z3, and it carries the counts). Anything else leaves the held run to go on with the time it had: JBMC can't write a trace as JSON from an SMT model, so a counterexample always comes from its own solver. Without a Z3, or with JVMCONTRACT_Z3=off, a run is as it was. doctor.py lists z3 as a tool whose absence limits what JBMC can prove.

Verified by the default test run (Rust and Python; the first run showed the attempt firing 50 ms into the short staged runs of two conformance tests, which is why it now waits 5 s at least), with unit tests of the reader and the lemmas and stand-in tests of a proof taken, a counterexample not taken with the run resumed where it was, and runs that never meet the attempt. One probe through jbmc::run with the real JBMC and Z3: lines.Lines#reprice ended Verified in 30.2 s (6 lemmas over 4 products, the attempt itself 0.2 s), and its defect twin was refuted by JBMC's own solver in 0.1 s as before. Not yet shown: the nine proof-tier tests of lib/tests/heap.rs, unchanged. Job 20261116-144006-vf-018-the-heap-proof-tier-under-jbmc-an runs them at the 600 s limit and is the finding's closing condition; VF-018 stays open until it is in. The prices test has proofs that are hard for Z3 too and may still need the longer limit.

commits.summary: A queued verification job starts at once: the commit announces it, a runner at work takes it into its run, and results are collected as they come (verification pending)
commits.body:
Until now the verification loop looked at the queue every 60 seconds while it waited, and not at all while a run was under way: pipeline.py run read the queue once, at its start, so a job committed during a long proof waited for that proof to end, and every result of a run was collected only after its longest job. The user asked that the prover, the watcher and the verifier work the queue together, with the intervals kept as the backup. The parts: (1) pipeline.py run reads the queue again at once after a nudge and every poll_seconds (30) besides, starts each new job beside the ones running as the budget allows, and ends after one last look when nothing runs and nothing is queued. (2) pipeline.py nudge says that the queue changed, by touching a file in the state directory; sync.py commit runs it when its commit changed verification/jobs/ or priorities.json, in both modes, so whoever queues a job announces it without having to remember. (3) verification-loop.sh, waiting for work, looks at once after a nudge. (4) pipeline.py wait blocks until a job has finished and waits to be collected, or no runner is at work, and /run-verification now collects, triages and commits each result as it comes while the other jobs run. (5) watch.py wait, the watcher's loop, announces a job it sees queued that nobody announced (once), and starts a verification loop if none is running while jobs wait, unless the watcher stopped it; watch.py verification nudge does the first by hand.

Reading the queue had to become cheap for this: it took 6.4 s here, a git process or two for each of 407 job files, and now takes 0.3 s, with one git cat-file for all the files and a source commit looked up only for jobs still waiting. The runner writes its pid into its lock file, so that wait and nudge can tell a runner is at work without trying the lock, which would turn away a runner starting at that moment.

Verified by the default test run (46 of 47 on the first run; the one failure was a test listing a commit's exact steps, updated and rerun with its neighbours), with new tests: a job committed during a run starts at a nudge and its result is collected before the run ends; without a nudge the interval finds it; the verification loop starts a run at a nudge long before its interval (stand-ins for the pipeline and for claude); a commit that queues a job tells the pipeline and one that does not stays quiet; the watcher announces once and restarts a loop that is gone. It is expected refuted on 6.1.13, established on 6.1.14, and refuted on a mutant that lowercases the field in the default locale again. commits.summary: Example 289 (CVE-2022-22978) set up from its catalog entry: line-terminator prefix claim and preservation frozen, replays pass
commits.body:
Example 289 was a catalog entry (revisions pinned, no tasks). It is now a deep negative packet, set up as llm-dlc/runtime.md's catalog entry brief asks, with 288 (the packet's shape) and 285 (its HttpServletRequest carrier) as models. The release pair is Spring Security 5.6.3 -> 5.6.4, from published JARs. Each release's RegexRequestMatcher.java is the exact-fix pair's blob (9264b56f, a334afc7). Every other class the matcher reaches is byte-identical in the two closures (Spring Framework 5.3.19 and 5.3.20). The release pair also hardens StrictHttpFirewall, in a commit before the fix; that is outside the matcher and the claims. sources.lock.json records the tags, blobs, ancestry and JAR hashes against Maven Central.

There are two claims and six tasks. The security claim covers a matcher built as RegexRequestMatcher(P + ".*", null, caseInsensitive), where P is a literal ASCII prefix. It must match every request whose documented URL (servletPath + pathInfo, then ? and the query) begins with P, line terminators included, exactly or ignoring US-ASCII case. It is expected refuted on 5.6.3, established on 5.6.4, and refuted on a mutant that leaves DOTALL out of the case-insensitive flags. Preservation: outside a URL in the namespace that holds a line terminator, both releases decide alike. The controls are an adapter, a request carrier, a driver, 36 probes and an independent oracle with a self-test.

Now stage 2 runs on every run, in the fixed session at high effort (was medium), on changes and on examples by number alike. Where a path sets no default the earlier stated assumption stands; a Locale the checker knows nothing of, a String outside ASCII and a comparison of two Locales by reference are named gaps or refusals. (2) A reference read from an array at a computed index is one symbolic reference among the cells, where it split the path per cell. commits.summary: Example 289: a pattern that is an input is modelled where the own checker shows it is a literal followed by .*, and the four frozen claims are queued through the adapter entry (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 289 is CVE-2022-22978 (Spring Security 5.6.3 to 5.6.4): RegexRequestMatcher compiled the rule it was given without Pattern.DOTALL, so /admin/.* did not match /admin/ followed by a line feed. Its two frozen claims quantify over the pattern (a literal prefix and .*), the case mode and every request String, so java.util.regex is on the proof's path with a pattern that is an input. The claims are unchanged.

The verifier's own checker (lib/src/bmc) gained one guarded rule and what the path needs beside it. regex.rs: Pattern.compile(String, int) of a String that is no constant is modelled only where the solver shows that on the path the String can only be characters that stand for themselves followed by .*; the Pattern is then those characters as a quoted text and . any number of times, and any other pattern stays the JDK's call, a gap refused by name. The flags CASE_INSENSITIVE and DOTALL are formulas (a constructor chooses them by an input, and paths that chose differently may have merged before the call); that no other flag is set is the solver's to show. One .* that ends an expression takes surrogates: what comes before it matched none, so it never begins inside a pair, and neither a pair nor a surrogate alone is a line terminator, so matching by unit is the JDK's matching by code point there; a dot anywhere else still makes an input with a surrogate the JDK's call. strings.rs: Character.isLetter of an ASCII char, the JDK's call of any other. runtime.rs: the java.util.logging levels below INFO as constants and Logger.isLoggable of one as false, under an assumption each outcome states (the matcher's debug line through spring-jcl is not written). models: IntStream.range(int, int) enters a model the checker runs (RangeStream), as String.chars() does.

Evidence for the rules: lib/tests/claims.rs has a new tool-tier test over a new fixture, claims.P. It proves the rule is its definition written out in Java (begins with the literal, ASCII case folded under CASE_INSENSITIVE, no line terminator after it without DOTALL) under each flag combination and with the flags chosen by an input, on every pattern and String of the bound; refutes a wrong claim on a witness run on a JVM; shows the refusals by name (any pattern, any text before the dot, another flag, a dot inside with a surrogate in the input, isLetter outside ASCII, isLoggable at INFO); and samples the definitions against the JDK on a JVM, with the five line terminators, surrogates alone and in pairs, the letters that fold outside ASCII, and isLetter on every char. lib/README.md and lib/models/README.md describe the rules.

The example: proofs/prove.py passes each frozen claim to jvmcontract through the adapter entry on the release's own bytecode, with no lemma and nothing put in a method's place, and builds the mutant by the replay route's recipe (the JAR it gives has the SHA-256 the mutant replay's receipt records). It follows loops for 26 turns where the default is 16: the allowed change reads a URL of up to 25 units, and at 16 the preservation check ended with no verdict, saying a loop was covered by an invariant. proofs/predicates.py compiles the claims' assumption, assertion and allowed change with javac and evaluates them on the 44 probes: they read each as controls/oracle.py does. target.json, example.json and the README record the queue, the probes and what became of the four predicted blockers.

Verified: inline probes at the frozen bound, each one capped run, gave every expected verdict (fixed-security established in 28 s, vulnerable-security and mutant-security refuted in 3 s each on witnesses run on a JVM, the mutant's with caseInsensitive true; preservation established in 47 s, and refuted at bound 3 with no allowed change). The unit tests (285) and the claims, values, pairing, conformance, loops, object_strings, string_literals, tiers and value_parameters tests pass; test_costs.py lint agrees; validate_example.py 289 passes. The default test run was not run: it is owed when the example is decided.

Jobs queued, the results of record: 20261116-214343-example-289-fixed-security-through-the-a, 20261116-214344-example-289-vulnerable-security-through, 20261116-214344-example-289-mutant-security-through-the, 20261116-214344-example-289-preservation-through-the-ada, and the proof tier after the engine changes, 20261116-214344-the-proof-tier-after-example-289-s-engin.

The proof tier after 288's engine changes passed (35m47s). 288's vulnerable-security and mutant-security ended on the checker's own 30-minute limit with no verdict, not with a wrong one; they are to be resubmitted larger in 288's next cycle, as its handoff says. commits.summary: Example 290: a library initializer the checker does not run is observed on a JVM, registrations are a LinkedHashMap in order and classes are found by name, and fixed-security is queued through the adapter entry (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 290 (CVE-2023-34035, Spring Security 5.8.4 to 5.8.5: requestMatchers(String...) chooses a matcher type by the servlet context's registrations) gets its proof script, proofs/prove.py, which passes the frozen claims to jvmcontract through the adapter entry on the releases' own bytecode, beside the route, and proofs/predicates.py, which shows that the claims' expressions as javac compiles them agree with the oracle on the 27 select probes. An inline probe established fixed-security at the frozen bound of 8 in 6.9 s (659 paths). It is queued as job 20261116-225709-example-290-fixed-security-through-the-a. The two refutations and preservation are not decided: target.json's handoff says where each stops (Collections.emptyMap, Arrays.asList, ArrayList's addAll and toArray; then the matchers' constructors).

What the verifier gained for it (lib/). The new kind: prove --observed-initializer CLASS (src/observed.rs, src/bmc/observed.rs). Spring's ClassUtils builds its tables through an IdentityHashMap, a HashSet and a map of soft references, which the checker does not run (identity hash order, a float load factor, reference queues), and the servlet API's GenericServlet and HttpServlet each load a resource bundle. Such an initializer has no input, so the tool runs it on a JVM instead: the class is initialized in a JVM of its own, first thing, on the check's class path, its static fields are read by reflection, and the checker takes that state where a use initializes the class. Held: null, integral and boolean primitives, Strings (and whether each is the pooled one), Classes, a java.util.HashMap of String keys (as the HashMap model's entries) and arrays of those; any other value is not held, and a read of such a field is refused by name. A result that used one states it among what it rests on: one observation on the check's JDK, taken to be what the initializer leaves in every run. It is asked for class by class, is refused with --cache and for an initializer that throws, and is never used for the class under proof: the registry's own initializer runs as written. A class of a JDK package that the class path holds (javax.servlet's) is the JDK's to the checker, initialized already; naming it as observed is how its initializer is now accounted for.

commits.summary: A proof by induction and a lemma's summary no longer stand in for a call that writes, throws, or reads what a caller can change
commits.body:
Three false proofs, each reproduced first on the checker as it was (lib/tests/fixtures/claims/claims/Effects.java, whose main prints what a JVM says): (1) prove --decreases on a method that counts its calls in a static field proved 'result == 1' where a JVM returns 2, because the induction hypothesis replaced the inner call and dropped its write; (2) with a throws clause, the hypothesis returned a value for an inner call the property itself says throws, and proved 'result == n' of a method that never returns; (3) a lemma about a getter, proved in the fresh state where its static field is 0, was used as a summary after the caller wrote the field, and proved 'result == 0' of a method that returns what it wrote. The same held through a callee, through an array a static field holds, for the default locale, and for a lemma whose own assertion reads a field.

Now: a method proved by induction is held to the write checks a summary's method already had (Options::own_induction says the proof is by induction alone, where reads are sound because the inner calls are made in the state of the call under proof); the hypothesis does not cover arguments on which a throws clause says the call throws (the induction then does not go through); a lemma's method, and the lemma's assumption and assertion, may read no static field that is not final, no non-final field or cell of an object that was there before the call, and not the default locale (Engine::reads); a summary is not used while its method's class is still being initialized. A lemma about a method of no parameters now compiles (its assertion is over the result alone).

Which existing results rest on these mechanisms: none uses prove --decreases directly; examples 286 and 288 use lemmas about PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(String,String), whose bytecode in the pinned 5.3.19 JAR reads no field and no array (javap), so their results did not rest on the hole; that the tightened checks still prove those lemmas is for a job to confirm. Verified by lib/tests/claims.rs (18 passed, among them the three new tests and the changed lemma test: a method that counts with calls++ is now refused at its read, one that only writes at its write), the summary unit tests, and test_costs.py run --changed (8 of 8 passed: cargo test's 33 binaries and three Python files).
